summary: Verified the new editable-content surface + live in-place editor for Overall Beauty & Wellness. Backend pytest: 67/70 passing (same 3 SMTP-not-configured failures as prev iteration — expected). Frontend: homepage marquee correctly says 'Hydrodermabrasion' (bare 'Hydroderm' does not appear); all 13 Studio Editor tabs (brand, banner, marquee, hero, manifesto, founder, services, consultation, mission, contact, testimonials, footer, legal) render without crashing and with zero console errors; marquee edit/add/remove + save persists via GET /api/content; Live Editor works for staff (99 [data-edit] elements armed on homepage, hero.line1 edit published + survived full reload, Cancel correctly reverted hero.line2); Live Editor is hidden on /studio and hidden for anonymous + non-staff clients; mobile 390px looks clean on / and /book. FOUND ONE REAL BUG: 'Reset all to defaults' does NOT actually clear overrides in the DB — server merges with $set instead of replacing the doc, so sending {} is a no-op.

critical.issue: Uses {'$set': {**data,...}} so sending an empty overrides body ({}) is a no-op. As a result, the Studio Editor's 'Reset all to defaults' button (which POSTs {}) shows a success toast but leaves the existing override keys (hero, marquee, banner, testimonials, etc.) in MongoDB. Users cannot actually revert. Fix: replace with replace_one({'id':'main'}, {'id':'main', **data, 'updated_at':..., 'updated_by':...}, upsert=True) — or explicitly unset removed keys.

minor.issue: Same 3 pytest SMTP tests fail because EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY / SMTP env vars are unset — expected in this preview env.
Still not implemented (carried over from iteration_3). Not used by any current UI, so low urgency.

integration_issues.flow: Studio Editor → Reset all to defaults
integration_issues.issue: Toast says 'Reverted to defaults.' but /api/content still returns overrides. Root cause is the backend PUT /api/content $set merge (see backend critical bug). To fully repro: log in as staff, in editor make any change and Save; click 'Reset all to defaults' → confirm; then curl /api/content → the override keys are still present.

action_items: Fix PUT /api/content to fully replace the overrides document (or explicitly $unset any keys not present in the incoming payload) so that 'Reset all to defaults' (which sends {}) actually clears MongoDB.
Optional cleanup: convert deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown to FastAPI lifespan; still emitting DeprecationWarnings during pytest.
critical_code_review_comments: PUT /api/content merge-vs-replace mismatch is the root cause of the reset bug — the frontend's computeDiff() only sends changed keys, which is fine, but 'reset' cannot express deletions with the current $set model. Backend should either accept a full replacement (replace_one) or a diff format that includes deletions.
StudioEditor.jsx is 1365 lines — worth splitting per-section tab components for maintainability.
liveEdit.jsx correctly gates via user?.role === 'staff' and via loc.pathname.startsWith('/studio') — verified: anonymous & client role never see the toolbar, and /studio never shows it.
server.py still 817 lines in one file; still using deprecated on_event.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% — 13/13 editor tabs render, live editor CRUD + cancel + role-gating all pass, only failure is 'Reset all to defaults' due to backend bug

The only outstanding issue is that PUT /api/content is a merge, not a replace, so 'Reset all to defaults' cannot clear overrides. After main agent fixes PUT /api/content (replace_one), re-run the reset test: as staff, make any change → Save → click Reset all to defaults → curl /api/content should return {}. Backend pytest baseline is 67/70; SMTP 3 failures are expected until EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY is configured.
rca_of_the_issue: PUT /api/content in /app/backend/server.py:612-623 does `db.content.update_one({'id':'main'}, {'$set': {**data, ...}}, upsert=True)`. When data={} (the reset payload from StudioEditor.resetAllToDefaults → saveOverrides({})), the $set only updates updated_at/updated_by and leaves all previously-set override keys intact. Fix: use `db.content.replace_one({'id':'main'}, {'id':'main', **data, 'updated_at':..., 'updated_by':...}, upsert=True)` so a `{}` payload truly clears overrides. Reproduction: `curl -X PUT -H 'Authorization: Bearer <staff>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"data":{}}' /api/content` after any prior save → response still contains prior override keys.
